chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Nothing pollutes the water except that which has flowing blood (i.e., a warm-blooded creature).

key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: Marfu' — a hadith transmission term meaning the narrator omitted intermediate links and attributed the saying directly to the Imam/Prophet.
key_terms.نَفْسٌ سَائِلَةٌ: Flowing/spurting blood — the technical criterion distinguishing warm-blooded vertebrates (whose impurity pollutes water) from cold-blooded creatures and insects (whose presence does not).
key_terms.يُفْسِدُ: To corrupt, make impure (najis) — the legal term for rendering water ritually unfit for use in worship.

ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Sadiq, what makes water ritually impure in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) lays down a foundational rule of Islamic ritual purity: water is only rendered impure (najis) by the carcass or bodily fluids of a creature that possesses flowing (spurting) blood — meaning warm-blooded vertebrates. This ruling distinguishes such animals from insects and cold-blooded creatures whose presence in water does not render it impure. The hadith is transmitted through Muhammad ibn Yahya in a marfu' chain (directly attributed to the Imam without citing intermediate links), reflecting its importance as a transmitted ruling in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, 
(It has been narrated) raising it from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It would not pollute the water except if it has a spurting blood for it (warm blooded mammal)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya in a marfu‘ manner has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Water does not become polluted because of the living things which do not have spurting blood when a cut is made in its body.’”
